name: Roc
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Roc is a hero of Irish legend. His life stands behind the love tale of Diarmait and Granne. Roc had an affair with the goddess Duibhne, wife of the sombre god Donn. A child came out of the affair. The outraged Donn, a wronged husband, crushed the infant's skull. Roc knew magic. He saved his child by changing it into a giant boar. The boar grew to monstrous size and made its home on Ben Bulben, the hill rising above the town of Sligo. Duibhne went back to Donn and bore another son, Diarmait. That son later died in battle with his own half-brother, the great boar.
